messages:
ana: quickstart sample app CI started failing after SDK bump, can someone take a look? repo: github.com/redwood/sample-apps/llm-quickstart

mike: saw this in my inbox earlier, what’s the symptom? failing tests or auth errors?

ana: failing tests + 401s from the embeddings call. curl against the REST endpoint works locally though.

jordan: can you paste the failing log lines?

ana: sure:
```
ERROR: 401 Unauthorized - missing Authorization header
at fetch (/usr/src/app/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.js:45:12)
```

ana: SDK is v0.12.3 in the sample app. locally i can curl the hosted API with `-H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\"` and it returns OK.

mike: interesting. our SDK should set Authorization header. are you using the new `apiKey` config or `token` env?

ana: env is REDWOOD_API_KEY (old quickstart env var). the SDK constructor in sample uses `new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })`

jordan: oh — SDK 0.12 changed header name mapping for legacy keys. it now prefers `token` and will send `X-Redwood-Key` when `apiKey` is passed, for backward compatibility with on-prem integrations. that was meant for Private deployments but it leaked into hosted behavior.

sara: wow. that would explain curl (which uses bearer) vs SDK (which sends X-Redwood-Key). Hosted API expects `Authorization: Bearer ...`.

mike: i remember that change. we added conditional header because some customers had special proxies. but we failed to gate it by deployment mode.

ana: also noticed a param mismatch in the embeddings call: sample app sets `timeout_ms` on SDK call, but REST query param is `timeout_seconds`. SDK sends raw int in ms so requests were timing out server-side.

jordan: so two issues: header mapping and timeout units. both could cause CI flakiness. thanks for catching.

mike: quick workaround for sample app: use raw REST call in the sample until SDK patch lands. e.g. replace with: 
```js
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-embed-1', input })
})
```

ana: will try that. can we also patch the sample app to use `token` env var as a short-term fix?

mike: yes, but we should fix SDK overall: behavior parity with REST for hosted mode. plan: 1) revert the header fallback for hosted deployments 2) normalize timeout parameter names/units (support both `timeout_ms` and `timeout_seconds`, prefer ms internally) 3) add e2e test that runs the quickstart against hosted sandbox.

sara: timeline?

mike: i'll open a PR for header revert + unit tests today, patch version 0.12.4. timeout normalization is a small change, will include in same PR if possible.

integrations-bot: created issue #4521: \"SDK: hosted header parity + timeout unit normalization (affects quickstart)\" assigned to @mike

jordan: also add a note in the SDK changelog and update quickstart README to recommend `REDWOOD_TOKEN` env var and show the fetch workaround.

ana: thanks. one more oddity: SDK retry behavior differs from REST docs. when the embeddings call hits 5xx the SDK retries twice by default; REST gateway will 429-throttle and include Retry-After which SDK didn't honor for that endpoint. we should ensure SDK honors Retry-After header.

mike: good catch — that will be included. policy: honor Retry-After for 429 and 503, and treat embedding POSTs as idempotent if a request-id is supplied.

sara: can someone temporarily patch CI to use the raw fetch snippet? our tests are blocked.

ana: i can push a quickfix. updating CI now, will mark the commit with `[quickfix]`

mike: thanks. i'll link the PRs here once open. once 0.12.4 is out we should backfill a migration note and bump quickstart to use the fixed SDK. :shipit: :eyes:
